question.text: How is CTT applied on the sale of a commodity option?

answer.text: At 0.05% on the option premium — payable by the seller
Levied on the full contract value
The same rate as equity STT

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the CTT schedule for commodity derivatives, on the sale of an option on a commodity, CTT is charged at 0.05% of the option premium and is payable by the seller. On exercise of a commodity option, CTT is charged on the settlement value and is payable by the purchaser — a separate charging event. The Trap: The sale event and the exercise event are two different charging points. CTT on sale is on the premium and falls on the seller; CTT on exercise is on the settlement value and falls on the purchaser. They are not the same charge. Note: Because the sale charge is calculated on the premium (not the contract value), CTT on selling an option is small relative to the underlying notional exposure.
